cases.name: Caroline "Carrie" Elizabeth Nosal
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Caroline had a giving disposition and a love of animals. Her heart enveloped others around her, reaching out to others in their times of isolation and need. She was deeply loved by her friends and family. With a keen mind, Caroline was an avid reader. She graduated from Sun Prairie High School in 2010 and attended college at Madison Area Technical College. An accomplished figure skater, and equestrian, Caroline's other interests included working with animals at the Humane Society, playing video games, and watching favorite TV series like Star Trek or Monty Python. She was employed at Metro Market, where she was an assistant produce manager."

cases.name: Christina Hatcher
cases.about:
She was a manager at an Applebee’s restaurant. Her mother, Angela Hatcher, said she always put her girls first. Hatcher and her daughters made frequent outings to Chuck E Cheese’s or to the park, her mother said. A band kid at heart — Hatcher played the trumpet in marching and concert band at Fairbanks High School in Milford Center, Ohio — she also instilled a love of music in her daughters. When she wasn’t busy working or with her daughters, Hatcher enjoyed socializing with friends. “She just liked to live life. She was a social butterfly,” Angela Hatcher said. Hatcher had a bright personality that will be greatly missed in her workplace, said Denise Harris, spokeswoman for Wisconsin Hospitality Group, which operates the Applebee’s where Hatcher worked. Hatcher earned a cosmetology certificate from a job training program while she was in high school, but a career in cosmetology took a backseat when one of her daughters was born. Recently, however, she had hoped to re-enroll in a program and make her way into the profession. “She was trying to better her life so she could better her kids’ life,” Angela Hatcher said.

“She was full of life and will never be forgotten,” Harris said. “Christina was beloved by all of the staff, management and many regular guests at her restaurant.”
cases.narrative: He allegedly strangled her and stabbed her in the neck with scissors. Dane County Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Vincent Tranchida described “sharp weapon defects” to the right and left side of Hatcher’s neck, along with bruises to her right and left arm, shoulders and upper chest. Hatcher also had a blackened and swollen right eye with broken blood vessels in the eye. Late Friday night, the medical examiner’s office said that Hatcher died from “homicidal sharp-force injuries.” Hatcher died from two stab wounds to her neck, though an autopsy also found numerous other injuries on her body that included blunt-force injuries to her torso, arms, legs, hands, fingers and eye.

cases.name: Patricia "Patty" Anne McCollough
cases.about:
She was a member of The Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa of the Ojibwa Native American Tribe.

Her obituary said, "Patty graduated from LaFollette High School, with the class of 1984. Following high school, she lived in Tampa Bay, Fla., for several years before eventually returning home to be closer to her family. When Patty was 27, she met Bob Lesch and three years later they started a family together. Patty was a loving mother and made their home a warm and welcoming environment to all of Brianna’s childhood friends.

Patty worked as a lunch lady at MMSD and as a server and/or manager for Lums, Cottage Cafe and Barbers Bay Resort. For the last several years of Patty’s life, she provided in-home care for her mother, Roberta. She also enjoyed the simple pleasures in life: crafts, knitting, crocheting and caring for children.

Patty was very proud of her daughter, Brianna, and enjoyed spending time with family and friends. Patty was the type of person who’s smile would light up a room. She had a big heart to help everyone who crossed her path and was always filled with contagious joy."

https://www.gundersonfh.com/obituaries/Patricia--McCollough-?obId=22442876
cases.narrative: On 9/16/2021, her body was discovered body in a bedroom with items including dresser drawers and televisions stacked on top of her, and could be seen from the adjoining hallway, at a house at 4517 Deerwood Drive in Madison, WI. Her autopsy report showed that she died of mechanical asphyxia and blunt force injuries of the torso. She suffered crushing, suffocating injuries that ultimately killed her, authorities said.
